Background:

D. Francisco de Almeida was the first viceroy of Portuguese India, who lived between 1453 and 1515. A few months before the battle of Diu, his son was captaining a ship when he was attacked by surprise by Meliqueaz, a mamluk commander fighting for an indian sultanate. His son was killed in that attack, and D. Francisco de Almeida was deeply affected by it, and the whole thing was "personal". It was so important to him, that he had his replacement that had just arrived from portugal inprisoned so he wouldn't stop him from getting revenge. (Afonso de Albuquerque, a legendary man responsible for portuguese strategy in the far east for the next 400 years)

The Letter:

I say onto you, o honored Meliqueaz, captain of Diu, and let you know that i am coming with my knights to this city of yours, to kill those who have taken refuge there, after in chaul fighting with my people, and killing a man that was my son; And i come with hope of god in heaven to take vengeance on them and those who have helped them; and if i do not find them, this city of yours will not escape me, and will pay me all, and you, for the good help you did in chaul; this i let you know, so that you are well aware for when i arrive, that i am coming, and that i am now in this island of Bombay, as will tell you the one carrying this letter to you.

There's plenty of sarcasm in the letter, such as when he calls meliquez honorable and calls what he did in chaul "good help" ( Though some of it may be both sincere as well as sarcastic, meliaquez treated well the portuguese prisioners taken in chaul, and returned them unharmed, but Franciscos son was not one of them, he died tied to the mast of his ship commanding his troops. )

The battle:

The battle of Diu was a resounding victory for the Portuguese troops, destroying the muslim/indian fleets and assuring Portuguese naval hegemony in the indian ocean for the next hundred years. The portuguese had 30 casualties and the indians/muslims had roughly 1500.
